repo.description:
### Summary

A partner can read the full metadata of every asset the sharer put in their Locked Folder. That
includes GPS coordinates, the on-disk path, the EXIF description and a thumbhash preview. The
partner gets it by calling the legacy search endpoints with the `visibility` field left out, while
their own session is unlocked with their own PIN.

The guard for this only fires when the client sends `visibility` explicitly. Leaving one optional
field out of the same request body gets past it.

| route | what the partner gets |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/search/metadata` | asset rows with `exifInfo` |
| `POST /api/search/statistics` | a count of the locked assets |
| `POST /api/search/random` | locked assets in the sample |
| `POST /api/search/large-assets` | locked assets listed |

Asset bytes stay protected. `GET /assets/{id}`, `/thumbnail` and `/original` are all refused, so this
is metadata rather than file access.

**How this differs from CVE-2026-108165.** That one is the partner sync stream:
`POST /api/sync/stream`, queried in `server/src/repositories/sync.repository.ts`. This is the search
path, queried in `server/src/utils/database.ts`. The two build their queries in different files and
share no code, so a fix to the sync queries will not change this behaviour. Both are present in
v3.3.3.

### Details

The legacy builder applies its visibility predicate conditionally:

```ts
// server/src/utils/database.ts:432-436
    .$if(!!options.visibility, (qb) =>
      options.visibility === 'not-locked'
        ? qb.where('asset.visibility', '!=', AssetVisibility.Locked)
        : qb.where('asset.visibility', '=', options.visibility!),
    )
```

`!!undefined` is `false`, so when `visibility` is omitted no visibility predicate is added at all.
The only ownership predicate in the builder is this:

```ts
// server/src/utils/database.ts:489
    .$if(!!options.userIds, (qb) => qb.where('asset.ownerId', '=', anyUuid(options.userIds!)))
```

and `userIds` still holds the partner ids, because the guard that strips them keys on the explicit
value:

```ts
// server/src/services/search.service.ts:356-360
  private async getUserIdsToSearch(auth: AuthDto, visibility?: AssetVisibility): Promise<string[]> {
    // Locked assets are personal. Never include partner IDs, regardless of A's elevated session.
    if (visibility === AssetVisibility.Locked) {
      return [auth.user.id];
    }
```

Five callers pass `undefined` as soon as the caller's own session is elevated
(`search.service.ts` lines 106, 128, 146, 161 and 193, each identical):

```ts
visibility: dto.visibility ?? (auth.session?.hasElevatedPermission ? undefined : 'not-locked'),
```

So for an elevated caller who omits the field there is no visibility filter, and
`ownerId IN (self, ...partners)`. Every partner's locked asset matches.

The V3 builder gets this right, which is where the fix should come from:

```ts
// server/src/utils/database.ts:814-816
      .where((eb) =>
        eb.or([eb('asset.visibility', '!=', AssetVisibility.Locked), eb('asset.ownerId', '=', scope.lockedOwnerId)]),
      )
```

That predicate is unconditional and scoped to the requester, so a locked row survives only if the
requester owns it. Sending `"filter": {}` routes to V3 and returns nothing, while the same query
without it leaks.

### Proof of concept

immich v3.3.1 in Docker. A is the victim, B the partner. A uploads an asset, sets a PIN, unlocks,
and sets the asset to `visibility: locked`. A shares with B. B turns it on in B's own timeline and
unlocks B's own session with B's own PIN. B never learns A's PIN, and holds no admin role, no API
key and no share link.

```http
POST /api/search/metadata
Authorization: Bearer <B, elevated session>

{"size":200,"withExif":true}
```

```json
{"assets":{"total":1,"items":[{
  "id":"fbf29e29-e631-486e-9b14-47c23fd31eb9",
  "ownerId":"b99e2116-db06-4613-9199-3cecb4bb33f1",
  "originalFileName":"secret-location.jpg",
  "visibility":"locked",
  "exifInfo":{"latitude":48.85837,"longitude":2.294481,"city":"Paris 16 Passy","description":"PRIVATE-DESCRIPTION-LEAK"}
}]}}
```

`ownerId` is A, not B. That is a cut-down view of the item for readability. Transcript `[5]` in
`EVIDENCE.txt` has the whole thing, including `originalPath`, `checksum` and `thumbhash`.

Controls, all on the same B session:

| request | result |
|---|---|
| `{"size":200}` before B unlocks B's own session | `total: 0` |
| `{"size":200,"visibility":"locked"}` | `total: 0`, the guard fires |
| `{"size":200,"filter":{}}`, which routes to V3 | `total: 0` |
| `GET /assets/<id>` and `/thumbnail` and `/original` | `400` and `400` and `404` |
| `/search/statistics {}` against `{"visibility":"locked"}` | `total: 1` against `total: 0` |

The web client reaches this with no request crafting. The "Review large files" page sends no
visibility:

```ts
// web/src/routes/(user)/utilities/large-files/[[photos=photos]]/[[assetId=id]]/+page.ts
const assets = await searchLargeAssets({ minFileSize: 0 });
```

A partner who has unlocked their own folder and opens that page sees the sharer's locked assets.
The search box itself is fine. It sends `visibility: AssetVisibility.Timeline` explicitly
(`web/src/routes/(user)/search/[[photos=photos]]/[[assetId=id]]/+page.svelte:143-146`).

The bundle has `docker-compose.yml`, `poc.sh`, `evidence.sh` and `EVIDENCE.txt` with all eight
exchanges. Both scripts create their own admin and their own A and B accounts, so they run against
an empty container.

### Impact

For each asset A put in the Locked Folder, B gets the id, `ownerId`, `originalFileName`,
`checksum`, `thumbhash`, timestamps and dimensions. B also gets `originalPath`, which exposes A's
user UUID and the server's storage layout. With `withExif:true` B gets the GPS latitude and
longitude, the reverse-geocoded place name, the camera make and model, and the free-text
description.

Recognised people are not exposed. `database.ts:262` scopes person rows to the requester.

The Locked Folder is where a user puts the photos they specifically want hidden, behind a PIN.
Partner sharing is for the ordinary timeline. A takes no action beyond the partnership A already
agreed to, and gets no signal that it happened.

One reason not to sit on this: the symptom is already public. Issue
[#31498](https://github.com/immich-app/immich/issues/31498) reported it on 2026-09-13 and a bot
closed it 27 seconds later as a likely duplicate, with no human triage.

### Fix

Give the legacy builder the predicate the V3 builder already has, so it cannot depend on what the
client sent:

```diff
--- a/server/src/utils/database.ts
+++ b/server/src/utils/database.ts
@@ export function searchAssetBuilderLegacy(
+    .where((eb) =>
+      eb.or([
+        eb('asset.visibility', '!=', AssetVisibility.Locked),
+        eb('asset.ownerId', '=', options.viewingUserId!),
+      ]),
+    )
     .$if(!!options.visibility, (qb) =>
```

`viewingUserId` is already on `AssetSearchBuilderOptions` (`search.repository.ts:60`) and is already
set to `auth.user.id` at all five callers, so nothing new needs threading through. It needs a
non-null guard for callers that leave it unset.

The smaller-looking fix, making the `getUserIdsToSearch` condition catch `undefined` as well, is
wider than it looks. Three other call sites pass no `visibility` at all: `getAssetsByCity`
(`search.service.ts:201`), `getSearchSuggestions` (`:207`) and the V3 scope builder (`:318`). All
three would silently lose partner assets.

A test is worth adding too. The one at `server/test/medium/specs/services/search.service.spec.ts:111`
is named for this exact case and passes against the vulnerable code, because it sends
`{ visibility: AssetVisibility.Locked }`. A sibling that omits the field would have caught this.

Present from v3.0.0 through v3.3.3 and on main. Confirmed on v3.3.1.

### Disclosure

Please request a CVE when you publish this. I am happy to retest a patch, and the severity call is
yours.

All testing was against a container I ran locally.

Reported by Asif Masood (A51F221B), Application Security Engineer.
repo.summary: Partner can read the sharer's Locked Folder metadata when a search request omits visibility
